title: Board-pattern readiness test — most-repeated question types
chapter: CBSE Class 12 Political Science (028) · all fifteen chapters, weighted by the 2026-27 theory marks
short_title: Class 12 Political Science (028) · Board-pattern readiness test
tagline: Practice questions modelled on past CBSE papers; not predictions of this year's paper.
disclaimer: Original questions written for Teraminds Academy from the NCERT textbooks prescribed for 2026-27, modelled on the most-repeated question types in CBSE board papers 2023–26 and the Sample Question Paper 2026-27 (see our Board Blueprint). A board-pattern readiness test for practice only: not a prediction of any exam and no promise of marks.
instructions: 40 questions. MCQ and assertion-reason: choose one option. Numeric: type a whole number (no units).

A1.name: A1 · The End of Bipolarity (6 marks)
A1.tip: Gorbachev: perestroika (restructuring) and glasnost (openness). December 1991: Russia, Ukraine and Belarus declared the USSR disbanded; CIS formed. Shock therapy: a rapid switch to capitalism, backed by the World Bank and IMF.
A1.ncert: NCERT Contemporary World Politics (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 1 The End of Bipolarity

A2.name: A2 · Contemporary Centres of Power (6 marks)
A2.tip: EU: Maastricht Treaty 1992, common currency euro. ASEAN: 1967 (Bangkok Declaration), five founding members, 'ASEAN Way'. China: open-door reforms from 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
A2.ncert: NCERT Contemporary World Politics (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 2 Contemporary Centres of Power

A3.name: A3 · Contemporary South Asia (6 marks)
A3.tip: SAARC set up in 1985. Nepal abolished its monarchy and became a democratic republic in 2008. Sri Lanka: the LTTE fought for a separate Tamil Eelam; the IPKF was sent in 1987.
A3.ncert: NCERT Contemporary World Politics (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 3 Contemporary South Asia

A4.name: A4 · International Organizations (6 marks)
A4.tip: UN: six principal organs; five permanent Security Council members with the veto (US, UK, France, Russia, China). IAEA (1957) promotes peaceful use of nuclear energy. India's case for permanent membership.
A4.ncert: NCERT Contemporary World Politics (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 International Organisations

A5.name: A5 · Security in the Contemporary World (6 marks)
A5.tip: Traditional security: deterrence, defence, balance of power, alliance building. Non-traditional/human security: threats to people (terrorism, epidemics, poverty, migration); 'freedom from want' and 'freedom from fear'. Cooperative security.
A5.ncert: NCERT Contemporary World Politics (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 5 Security in the Contemporary World

A6.name: A6 · Environment and Natural Resources (6 marks)
A6.tip: Rio Earth Summit 1992 → Agenda 21. Kyoto Protocol 1997: targets for industrialised countries; India and China were exempt. CBDR: common but differentiated responsibilities. Global commons: atmosphere, oceans, Antarctica, outer space.
A6.ncert: NCERT Contemporary World Politics (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 6 Environment and Natural Resources

A7.name: A7 · Globalisation (4 marks)
A7.tip: Globalisation = flows of ideas, capital, commodities and people across the world. Cultural effects: homogenisation (spread of Western culture, 'McDonaldisation') and heterogenisation (cultures mixing and enriching each other).
A7.ncert: NCERT Contemporary World Politics (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 7 Globalisation

B1.name: B1 · Challenges of Nation-Building (6 marks)
B1.tip: 565 princely states; Hyderabad joined in 1948 after military action; Manipur's merger in 1949. States Reorganisation Commission (1953) → States Reorganisation Act 1956: 14 states and 6 union territories.
B1.ncert: NCERT Politics in India since Independence (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 1 Challenges of Nation Building

B2.name: B2 · Era of One-Party Dominance (4 marks)
B2.tip: First general election 1951-52, conducted under the first Chief Election Commissioner Sukumar Sen. Congress dominance rested on being a social and ideological coalition.
B2.ncert: NCERT Politics in India since Independence (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 2 Era of One-Party Dominance

B3.name: B3 · Politics of Planned Development (2 marks)
B3.tip: Planning Commission 1950. The Second Five Year Plan, drafted under P.C. Mahalanobis, stressed heavy industries.
B3.ncert: NCERT Politics in India since Independence (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 3 Politics of Planned Development

B4.name: B4 · India's External Relations (6 marks)
B4.tip: Panchsheel (1954, Nehru and Zhou Enlai). War with China 1962; Tashkent Agreement (1966) after the 1965 war with Pakistan; first nuclear test at Pokhran in 1974.
B4.ncert: NCERT Politics in India since Independence (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 India's External Relations

B5.name: B5 · Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System (4 marks)
B5.tip: 1967 elections: 'non-Congressism' (Ram Manohar Lohia). Congress split 1969. 1971: Indira Gandhi's 'Garibi Hatao' won a big majority.
B5.ncert: NCERT Politics in India since Independence (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 5 Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System

B6.name: B6 · The Crisis of Democratic Order (4 marks)
B6.tip: Emergency declared on 25 June 1975 under Article 352 (internal disturbance). After 1977, the Janata government set up the Shah Commission to inquire into the Emergency's excesses.
B6.ncert: NCERT Politics in India since Independence (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 6 The Crisis of Democratic Order

B7.name: B7 · Regional Aspirations (6 marks)
B7.tip: Punjab: Rajiv Gandhi–Longowal Accord 1985. Mizoram: Mizo Accord 1986 (Laldenga), statehood 1987. Dravidian movement: E.V. Ramasami 'Periyar'. Jammu and Kashmir, Assam and the North-East.
B7.ncert: NCERT Politics in India since Independence (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 7 Regional Aspirations

B8.name: B8 · Recent Developments in Indian Politics (8 marks)
B8.tip: From 1989: end of Congress dominance and the coalition era. Mandal Commission recommendations implemented in 1990 by the National Front government. Rise of the BJP. Growing consensus: new economic policy, OBC claims, role of state parties, pragmatism over ideology.
B8.ncert: NCERT Politics in India since Independence (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 8 Recent Developments in Indian Politics
